The day after his biggest win, he wanted to quit. 🔥

Elijah had just seen fire fall on Mount Carmel. Then one threat from Jezebel, and he ran into the wilderness, sat under a juniper tree and said, “It is enough” (1 Kings 19:4). God didn't lecture him. He gave him sleep, food, a still small voice, and the truth: 7,000 others had stayed faithful. He was never alone.

Ever felt like Elijah under that tree? Yes or no 👇

In 2 Kings 6, one of the sons of the prophets loses an axe head in the Jordan and cries, “Alas, master! for it was borrowed.” Elisha asks, “Where fell it?”, throws a stick in at that spot, “and the iron did swim.” God cares about the small things too.

A guy fell asleep during Paul's sermon. It's in the Bible. 😴

Hidden details #2: Eutychus falls from a third-floor window during a long sermon (Acts 20:9), Jesus writes on the ground twice (John 8:6-8), King Og's bed was made of iron (Deuteronomy 3:11), people lined the streets hoping Peter's shadow would pass over them (Acts 5:15), and a young man fled Gethsemane without his clothes (Mark 14:52).

Which one did you already know? Comment 1 to 5 👇

Lydia, a seller of purple from Thyatira, was at a riverside prayer meeting in Philippi when Paul spoke. “The Lord opened” her heart (Acts 16:14). She was baptized with her household and opened her home to Paul and his team. One of the first believers in Philippi.
